subject: reasoning
question: Gautam starts from point Y and drives 34 km towards the east. He then turns right, drives 68 km, then turns right again and drives 55 km. He then turns right and drives 11 km. He then turns right again, drives 81 km. He then turns left, drives 57 km and stops at point Z. How far (the shortest distance) and in which direction should he drive to reach point Y again? (Unless specified, all turns are 90-degree turns only.)
solution:
Given:

Gautam starts from point Y and drives 34 km towards the east. He then turns right, drives 68 km, then turns right again and drives 55 km. He then turns right and drives 11 km. He then turns right again, drives 81 km. He then turns left, drives 57 km and stops at point Z. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47226ec45b7dabe0f57573bb89570212a69d1c7aa8cd2f426403cc8d20c64eb5.png] 

Point Z is 60 km East of point Y. To reach point Y again, he must drive **60 km towards the West**.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**
